BetterGov Fellowship 2026 · Basic Education and Early Childhood

Local education spending, next to learning and child outcomes

This is my proposal for two challenges: Basic Education, set by DepEd and the Evidence for Education Coalition, and Early Childhood, set by EDCOM 2. The rest of this site is the prototype I built for it, on Naga City's public data.

The problem

The Basic Education challenge asks for Project Bukas school-level outcomes to be linked with local education budgets, so allocation is more efficient and equitable. The Early Childhood challenge asks for stunting, early literacy and child development centre data to be connected with government programs and investments through DBM COMPASS.

The missing piece in both is local spending. LGUs fund schools and young children through the Special Education Fund, nutrition programs and child development centres. That spending lives in each city's Annual Investment Program and budget ordinance, as PDFs or spreadsheets, with no school IDs, no barangay codes and no link to outcomes. So a Local School Board can't easily answer "Are we spending where learners are struggling?", and a coalition can't answer "Did the barangays without a CDC get one in this year's budget?" COMPASS currently stops at national transfers to LGUs.

Naga shows what happens when someone does the linking by hand. Its City School Board used Project Bukas to realign the SEF towards remediation and furniture, and the share of low emerging readers fell from 40% to 4% (as the Evidence for Education Coalition reports it). I want to make that analysis repeatable without a dedicated team for every LGU.

What I'll build

An open data layer and a decision view that put LGU education and early-childhood spending next to learning and child outcomes, tested on Naga City first.

At its centre is a local spending schema. It tags each LGU program by fund (SEF, General Fund, GAD), sector, target group and place (DepEd school ID, PSGC barangay code), plus the city's own planning frame, such as Naga's finish lines. Pipelines load the LGU's published AIP and budget ordinance, Project Bukas school data and the ECCD indicators (OPT+ stunting, CRLA literacy, CBMS child development centre gaps), joined on school ID and PSGC. Every figure carries its source document, reporting period and validation status, and anything that can't be matched is listed, not dropped.

From there, each tagged program is followed to its procurement plan items and the matching PhilGEPS notices and awards, each link with a match confidence. A decision view lets a Local School Board or a local ECCD coalition drill down from city to district to school or barangay, and from program to amount to contract. An MCP server over the same API lets COMPASS, the EDCOM 2 dashboard and AI assistants ask these questions and get answers with citations.

What already works

Before applying, I wanted to see how far Naga's public data actually goes, so I built the slice on this site. It reads the City's enacted 2026 budget and its 2027 AIP from the portal's public pages, tags each education and early-childhood row, and sets them beside DepEd's files for all 45 public schools in the Schools Division of Naga City (47,176 learners), keyed by school ID and PSGC barangay code.

Three things came out of it. The 2027 AIP puts ₱278.7 million into education and early childhood, and ₱130,000,000 of that (47%) is one SEF row that names no school. Of the 47 rows I tagged, 0 name a school or barangay. And DepEd's files already show where some SEF money lands: 28 school staff paid from the City SEF and 306 ICT items bought with LGU or SEF money in SY 2023-24.

To check it isn't a Naga-only trick, I ran the same thing on Zamboanga City and Cagayan de Oro, reading their 2026 ordinances from PDF. Zamboanga's book names 44 national high schools in their own sheets (₱11.6 million), and 42 of them now join to a DepEd school ID, so its money can be followed to a school. In Cagayan de Oro, 30 of 80 barangays have no child development centre on EDCOM 2's list, next to ₱1.0 million of day care and ECCD lines in the budget. All three cities' whole budgets are on the LGU budget comparison.

The outcome side turned out to be public as well, once I found where it lives. EDCOM 2's Early Childhood Dashboard carries school-level CRLA for 30 of Naga's 31 public elementary schools: 4.6% of learners read at the Low Emerging level at the end of SY 2025-26, from 2.0% (Naga North) to 6.4% (Naga South) by district. Stunting (OPT+ 2025) is published for the city as a whole (1.8%) but not by barangay, and child development centres only as a list of barangays without one, which none of Naga's is on. The site leaves the missing pieces empty and says so, and the checks page lists every record that didn't join. Getting barangay-level OPT+ and CDC counts from their owners is the first month's work.

How it connects to DBM COMPASS

Shared identifiers do the joining: DepEd school IDs, PSGC, UACS and LGU chart-of-accounts codes, and PhilGEPS reference numbers. With them, COMPASS's Local Government section and its LGSF and NTA data can sit beside each LGU's own SEF and early-childhood spending, and EDCOM 2's dashboard and Project Bukas can join to it. Every figure follows COMPASS's control rule, traceable to its source, reporting period and validation status, with completeness and refresh cadence stated per dataset.

The project ships an open API (OpenAPI 3.1), bulk CSV and Parquet downloads with Frictionless metadata, and an MCP server for COMPASS's MCP-compatible integrations. You can try the prototype's API on the Data & API page. I'll adopt the conventions the COMPASS, DepEd and EDCOM 2 teams set in sprint one. Code is AGPL v3; data is released under an open licence the data owners approve.

December to March
  1. December Agree the pilot questions with DepEd and E4E, EDCOM 2, the COMPASS team and Naga's City School Board. Get the data. Publish schema v0 and the crosswalk of school IDs and PSGC codes.
  2. January Tag Naga's education and early-childhood programs, load Bukas and the ECCD indicators, run the first PPMP-to-PhilGEPS match, and ship the API and downloads with a public list of anything that couldn't be matched.
  3. February Build the drill-down view, test it with the City School Board and a local ECCD coalition, and add the MCP server.
  4. March Run the schema on a second LGU's budget, write the documentation and a note on extending it to health, and Demo Day.

The data owners decide what is public, so I'll only publish what they have released or approved. Unmatched spending is reported as a result.

Separate from Stride's work

I'm the CTO of Stride Technologies, which builds the People's Budget Portal with WeSolve and the City. This fellowship work is separate from that contract and adds to it. It uses only published data (here, the portal's public pages and DepEd's open files), builds its own open layer in its own repository, and I'll report it that way.
